<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z ≈ 100.0524, which matches the monoisotopic mass of the formula C₅H₈O₂ (exact mass = 100.05243). This formula has a double‑bond equivalent of 2, indicating either a carbonyl plus a double bond or a ring. The most common small organic molecules with this formula are methyl acrylate (CH₂=CH‑COOCH₃) and pent‑2‑enoic acid (CH₃‑CH=CH‑COOH). Both fit the formula, but methyl acrylate is a simple ester that often appears in such tasks. I will verify with NMR and IR data, but the likely SMILES is “C=COC(=O)C”.</thought>
<final_answer>C=COC(=O)C</final_answer>
